[page[title]]

The source file must live in the standard folder for its element type.

What The Standard says

“Organization” — The Standard gives brokers a deliberate file organization, including partial files split by entity. Broker source should live where that architectural role and entity ownership are visible. read it here.
“Organization” — The Standard places API controllers under the Controllers folder and namespace. This establishes that element type as part of the source's required structural location. read it here.
“Organization” — The Standard gives web components a clear domain-driven Views structure for navigation, consistency and scalability. The analyser generalizes these explicit organization rules across recognized Standard element types. read it here.

Why it matters

The Standard's folder structure is a map of architectural responsibility. Placing a source file in the folder for its element type makes dependency direction reviewable from the tree and prevents correctly named classes from being hidden in misleading locations.

Bad code example

// Violates STXSTRUCT001: The source file must live in the standard folder for its element type.
// Services/StudentBroker.cs
class StudentBroker { }

Good code example

// Follows STXSTRUCT001
// Brokers/StudentBroker.cs
class StudentBroker { }
